headlines.raw_title: United Russia consolidates its leadership in parliamentary polls — Putin
headlines.title: United Russia consolidates its leadership in parliamentary polls — Putin
headlines.full_text: United Russia consolidates its leadership in parliamentary polls — Putin The Russian president emphasized that the party now bears even greater responsibility for legislation and "overall outcome" MOSCOW, September 28. /TASS/. The United Russia party has consolidated its leadership after the parliamentary elections and now bears even greater responsibility, Russian President Vladimir Putin said. "Following the elections, United Russia has solidified its leadership. This means that the responsibility for the course and dynamics of the legislative process, as well as for the overall outcome will become even greater," he said at a meeting with the leaders of political parties. "I am sure that United Russia will build comradely, partner cooperation with other factions, as it did before, and will ensure the traditionally effective and fair representation of all political forces in the Duma governing bodies and parliamentary committees," he added.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article simply reports Putin’s statement about United Russia’s strengthened leadership without bias or emotional language.

headlines.raw_title: Foreign special services’ attempts to derail elections in Russia failed — Putin
headlines.title: Foreign special services’ attempts to derail elections in Russia failed — Putin
headlines.full_text: Foreign special services’ attempts to derail elections in Russia failed — Putin The head of state stressed that Russia’s people had defended the sovereign right to decide about their own future MOSCOW, September 28. /TASS/. Foreign special services tried to derail the elections in Russia but failed to do that, Russian President Vladimir Putin said. "All attempts to disrupt the election campaign and interfere in our domestic affairs have completely failed. It is well known that such attempts, including those involving terrorist methods and the use of foreign intelligence services, were planned and carried out. But our people have defended the sovereign right of the Russian citizens to decide about their own future," he said at a meeting with the leaders of the parties that won seats in the State Duma, or lower house of parliament, during the recent elections.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece attributes election disruption to foreign special services, positioning them as the source of the problem.

headlines.raw_title: Central Election Commission chairwoman thanks Putin for decisions ensuring safe voting
headlines.title: Central Election Commission chairwoman thanks Putin for decisions ensuring safe voting
headlines.full_text: Central Election Commission chairwoman thanks Putin for decisions ensuring safe voting Ella Pamfilova said that decisions were made and relevant instructions were issued in a timely manner MOSCOW, September 28. /TASS/. Central Election Commission Chairwoman Ella Pamfilova thanked Russian President Vladimir Putin for timely decisions that helped ensure voting security under difficult conditions. "On behalf of my colleagues, let me thank you for the fact that a number of decisions were made and relevant instructions were issued in a timely manner," Pamfilova said at a meeting with the president. According to her, this enabled the Central Election Commission, together with the Defense Ministry, National Guard, Federal Security Service, Interior Ministry, Emergencies Ministry and other agencies, to take the necessary measures to ensure that voting took place under the safest possible conditions. "This is very important. And many thanks. We really managed to achieve this," the Central Election Commission chairwoman stressed.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It simply records the chairwoman's gratitude toward the president, lacking critical analysis.

headlines.raw_title: Western assessments of Russian elections hold little importance for CEC — official
headlines.title: Western assessments of Russian elections hold little importance for CEC — official
headlines.full_text: Western assessments of Russian elections hold little importance for CEC — official Ella Pamfilova stressed that during the election campaign, the Central Election Commission did its utmost to honor the basic principles of openness and transparency of the electoral system MOSCOW, September 28. /TASS/. Russia’s Central Election Commission (CEC) doesn’t take into account Western countries' assessments of Russian elections, as it considers domestic recognition of the election results to be the most important factor, CEC Chairwoman Ella Pamfilova said. "The West a priori refused to recognize our elections. That's not our concern. What matters is people’s support," she said at a meeting with President Vladimir Putin. She stressed that during the election campaign, the Central Election Commission did its utmost to honor the basic principles of openness and transparency of the electoral system, despite the difficult conditions the voting took place under. According to Pamfilova, people’s active involvement demonstrated their understanding of the significance of the elections for the country. She noted that for the first time since 2003, all of the CEC members, including those who represent parliamentary parties, shared a consolidated view on the results of the parliamentary campaign. This fact, in her words, means that all the participants in the political process recognize the election outcome. Elections to the Russian State Duma, or lower house of parliament, of the ninth convocation were held on September 18-20.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It frames Western assessments as irrelevant, omitting counterpoints.

headlines.raw_title: Putin thanks CEC chair for conducting elections at highest level
headlines.title: Putin thanks CEC chair for conducting elections at highest level
headlines.full_text: Putin thanks CEC chair for conducting elections at highest level The Russian leader noted that, regrettably, the election campaign did not pass without casualties among election commission staff MOSCOW, September 28. /TASS/. During a meeting with Central Election Commission Chairwoman Ella Pamfilova Russian President Vladimir Putin thanked her and all election commission staff for conducting the elections in Russia at the highest level. The Russian leader noted that, regrettably, the election campaign did not pass without casualties among election commission staff – a fact known to the entire country. "I would like to thank you and all election commission staff at every level for doing a good job – which is vitally important and necessary for the country. It was carried out at the highest level, particularly in terms of organization. It is crucial that the elections were also organized at the highest level from the legal standpoint," Putin. Elections of the 9th State Duma took place during a three-day voting period from September 18 to 20. For the first time, residents of the Donbass and Novorossiya regions participated in the elections. Ten parties were included in the electoral lists for the federal constituency: United Russia, the CPRF, the LDPR, New People, A Just Russia, the Russian Party of Pensioners for Social Justice, Communists of Russia, Rodina, the Russian Ecological Party "The Greens," and the Party of Direct Democracy. United Russia secures 349 seats; the CPRF – 37; the LDPR – 23; New People – 19; A Just Russia – 17; and Rodina – 1. Four independent candidates also win seats.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article praises the election process as conducted at the highest level, reinforcing national pride.

headlines.raw_title: Russia faced external difficulties during legislative polls — Putin
headlines.title: Russia faced external difficulties during legislative polls — Putin
headlines.full_text: Russia faced external difficulties during legislative polls — Putin The head of state said that the elections had taken place across all of Russia’s 89 constituent entities MOSCOW, September 28. /TASS/. During its recent legislative polls, Russia had to counter obstacles created from abroad, Russian President Vladimir Putin said during a meeting with the head of the country’s Central Election Commission (CEC), Ella Pamfilova. At the beginning of the meeting, Putin said that the elections had taken place across all of Russia’s 89 constituent entities. "This huge task involved not only organizing everything related to the voting process, it also entailed the need to overcome difficulties engineered against us from abroad, and it was associated with risk," Putin said.
headlines.llm_reasoning: President Putin frames electoral obstacles as engineered from abroad, blaming external actors.

headlines.full_text: Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression. Just a few months ago, Russia's war was an distant reality for many people in Europe outside of Ukraine. If Russian drones occasionally entered the airspace of countries like Poland or Romania, even official statements seemed strangely dismissive and abstract. Even after aRussian drone struck a high-rise apartment buildingin the eastern Romanian city of Galati in late May this year, many EU and NATO representatives hesitated to accuse Russia of intentional action. At most, there wasdiscussion of hybrid warfare. The situation has changed radically since the summer. Drone overflights have become almost daily in certain parts of central and southeastern Europe, and there have even been crashes and explosions, particularly in countries bordering Ukraine. Alerts are becoming more frequent, with authorities increasingly having to close airspace or suspend operations at airports, as unauthorized flights are detected. Russia has been bombing border crossings, infrastructure and trains in Ukraine, but very close to other borders.Acts of sabotage are also increasingly common. For the Baltic states,Poland, Moldova and Romania in particular, the war has long ceased to be "hybrid." More and more,politicians in these countries are saying that Russia is acting deliberately. headlines.full_text: Russian embassy warns NATO of armed conflict risk in case of Kaliningrad’s blockade Russia has necessary means to repel potential aggression and "stands ready to deploy its entire available arsenal of weapons," the diplomats said BRUSSELS, September 28. /TASS/. The Russian embassy in Belgium has warned NATO that the alliance’s irresponsible policy regarding Russia’s Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad heightens the risk of a direct military confrontation because Moscow is ready to use its entire arsenal of weapons to defend its territory if NATO tries to block the region. "Amid the aggressive policy pursued by NATO leadership and member countries, the embassy has conveyed our principled approaches to the NATO International Secretariat and the Belgian Foreign Minisry," reads a statement by the Russian Embassy to Belgium, which is in charge of diplomatic contacts with the North Atlantic alliance. "We warned that this reckless and irresponsible approach sharply increases the risks of a direct military confrontation with our country." "We emphasized that Russia possesses the necessary means to repel potential aggression and stands ready to deploy its entire available arsenal of weapons if NATO countries try to isolate the Kaliningrad Region from the rest of our country," Russian diplomats said. "We called upon the bloc’s member states to refrain from further escalatory rhetoric and actions in order to prevent a large-scale confrontation," the embassy added.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The embassy emphasizes Russia's strength and readiness to defend, portraying it as morally superior.

headlines.full_text: Ukraine considers moving critical enterprises underground to metro stations According to the Verkhovna Rada member, Russia essentially has complete control over the skies above Kiev MOSCOW, September 28. /TASS/. The Verkhovna Rada, Ukraine’s parliament, has proposed considering the relocation of critical enterprises to the country’s western regions and using underground metro tunnels for their operations. "Perhaps we should consider moving critical institutions and enterprises to western Ukraine and start assessing our underground tunnels and metro systems for the work of critical infrastructure," Rada member Alexey Goncharenko (designated as a terrorist and extremist in Russia) wrote on Telegram. He said that Russia essentially had complete control over the skies above Kiev. "I don’t know what verdict this is on the authorities. We probably need to do something," he concluded, noting that "an ordinary Shahed drone, not a jet-powered one," had hit the building of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine. A new series of explosions occurred in the Ukrainian capital on Monday. Ukraine’s Novosti.Live reported damage to a strategic facility in Kiev’s Podolsky district. A fire in the National Academy of Sciences building in central Kiev had still not been extinguished.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It portrays Russia as having complete control over Kiev’s skies, urging drastic defensive measures.

An Istanbul court has convicted a popular comedian of insulting President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan – and handed down a sentence of almost 19 months – but ordered his release due to time served. It has also placed him under a travel ban, preventing him from travelling outside Turkey. A final decision in the case will come from the court of appeals. Deniz Göktaş - who denied the charges - has already spent nearly 90 days in prison. Prosecutors had asked for up to 12 years. His case comes amid a wave of arrests in Turkey that human rights groups say is aimed at crushing dissent. His stand-up routine went viral on YouTube, attracting more than 15 million views. Prosecutors had singled out a line in which the comedian called the Turkish leader "a shy dictator", but Göktaş insisted there was "no criminal element" in his comments. "Dictator is not an insult," he said, "it is a political characterisation." But angering the president in Turkey is not funny. Göktaş was arrested and handcuffed at Istanbul airport in July when he returned from a holiday. Visitors write down their names, sometimes add an ID card number, and sign to say that nobody forced or enticed them to attend church. The forms, a copy of which the BBC has seen, have no official standing. Churches keep them in case a prayer meeting is challenged and its organisers are accused of trying to convert those inside. The practice began at some churches in late August, just before a new law against religious conversion took effect in Maharashtra state, of which Mumbai is the capital. The law prohibits religious conversions brought about by force, fraud, coercion or inducement. It also requires people who want to convert voluntarily to notify authorities in advance. An unlawful conversion can lead to a prison sentence of up to seven years, rising to 10 for a repeat offence. Maharashtra's government says the law protects people, particularly those who are socially or economically vulnerable, from being forced or deceived into changing their religion. headlines.full_text: First group of migratory pelicans spotted in northwestern Iran TEHRAN – The first group of migratory pelicans has been spotted at Solduz Wetland in Naqadeh County, northwestern Iran. TEHRAN – The first group of migratory pelicans has been spotted at Solduz Wetland in Naqadeh County, northwestern Iran. Akbar Qaemi, head of the Naqadeh Department of Environment, said a group of 35 pelicans had arrived at the wetland as part of their seasonal migration from northern areas toward warmer southern regions, IRNA reported. He noted that the number of migratory pelicans at the wetland is expected to increase in the coming days, adding that most of the birds observed so far are juveniles that were born in Lake Urmia National Park and its surrounding areas and have begun their seasonal migration as temperatures fall. In addition to migratory pelicans, various species of resident and migratory birds, including sandpipers, stilts, gulls, garganeys, coots, herons, and different species of ducks, are currently being observed at Solduz Wetland. Naqadeh County is home to seven seasonal and permanent wetlands, which annually provide habitat for more than 10,000 migratory and resident birds. Iran is the most important country in West Asia in terms of housing migratory birds in winter, as around two million birds fly each year to spend winter in the country’s wetlands, according to an official with the Department of Environment. Encompassing numerous wetlands, reservoirs, and diverse water bodies, Iran welcomes millions of migratory birds every year. In reality, diabetes poses a threat to almost everyone in the modern world. Some nations are already managing the crisis more effectively than others. To begin with, it is important to note that there are two types of diabetes. Type 1 diabetes often develops during childhood or young adulthood, though it can appear at any age. It is not caused by a high-sugar diet or excess weight. The first crewed flight of Boeing’s Starliner spacecraft since 2024 is planned by 2028, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said. Before launching the spacecraft with a crew, NASA plans to conduct an uncrewed Starliner flight to the International Space Station (ISS) in 2027, followed by a crewed mission. The current plan is to return astronauts to Starliner-2 by 2028, Isaacman said at a press conference in Florida. Astronauts Barry Eugene Wilmore and Sunita Williams arrived at the ISS aboard Starliner, which launched on June 5, 2024. It was the first crewed launch of Boeing’s spacecraft to the space station. Wilmore and Williams were initially expected to remain in orbit until June 18. Their return was later postponed, first until June 26 and then indefinitely, due to a spacecraft malfunction involving the failure of several maneuvering thrusters during docking with the ISS. Starliner undocked from the ISS without a crew on September 7, 2024, and landed six hours later at the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. Wilmore and Williams returned to Earth on March 19, 2025, as part of the crew of a Crew Dragon spacecraft operated by US company SpaceX.

In addition to water loss due to anintense multiyear drought, the US Geological Survey and the Bureau of Reclamationreport found, Lake Powell faced an average annual loss in storage capacity of about 33,270 acre-feet, or 11 billion gallons, per year between 1963 and 2018. That’s enough water to fill the Reflecting Pool on the National Mall about 1,600 times. The capacity of the reservoir is shrinking because of sediments flowing in from theColorado and San Juan rivers, according to the report. Those sediments settle at the bottom of the reservoir and decrease the total amount of water the reservoir can hold. As of Monday, Lake Powell was around 25% full, according to data from the Bureau of Reclamation. It’s bad news for a region already facing water shortages and extreme wildfires due to the drought. headlines.full_text: Inside Yemen's front-line city as Houthis battle for control In rare access to Yemen's conflict zone the BBC travels to the front line with pro-government soldiers. "This is the first drone," said the soldier accompanying us in south-western Yemen. "It's usually followed by an attack." The buzzing sound overhead got louder as we took cover under the bushes, before climbing back into the vehicle and driving away. Within about 10 minutes, the loud thuds of strikes followed, one after another, though it was unclear where they landed. It is hard to tell where the front line begins in the mountains south-west of the city of Taiz. Saudi-backed pro-government forces are battling to push back Houthi fighters, who swept down the coast of the Red Sea earlier this month, taking control of a key shipping chokepoint and escalating Yemen's civil war. We travelled with government forces from Taiz through checkpoints to the line where their control ends and no man's land begins, in order to see the fighting up close. Homes are scattered across the slopes, but many stand abandoned after families fled to escape the fighting. It is eerily quiet, no sound of the cars or motorbikes that are continuously whizzing through the city. All you can hear is the bleating of livestock and the sound of incoming and outgoing fire. Bailey's exit occurs twelve months following his assumption of the position, representing another significant leadership transition at the law enforcement organization under FBI DirectorKash Patel'sadministration. Bailey, formerly serving asMissouri'sattorney general, assumed the position in August last year and initially shared the deputy director responsibilities with Dan Bongino. In December, Bongino also resigned after disagreements with then-Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding the management of the Epstein case materials. "With great pride in what we have accomplished, I am announcing that I am stepping down to return to my family in Missouri," Bailey said in a post. "I am confident Director Patel will continue to reform the FBI, combat violent crime, defend the homeland, ensure strong organizational accountability and restore public trust in this institution of excellence."
